name: halflife-mcp
description: Local, file-backed long-term memory for coding agents. Stores typed memories (preference, procedural, fact, episodic, trace) as Markdown files with a derived SQLite index; recall is keyword + graph, plus optional local vectors. Memories decay by half-life; inferred ones stay provisional until confirmed. It sees only explicit tool calls, never the transcript. Five tools are read-only; remember and reinforce write local files; forget deletes. Off until you turn it on.
saferAlternatives: memory_brief, memory_recall, memory_get, memory_list and memory_stats are read-only (readOnlyHint: true): from 0.1.2 they never write, move or delete memory files and only refresh the derived SQLite index.
memory_remember and memory_reinforce write Markdown files under HALFLIFE_HOME; writes that look like secrets are refused.
memory_forget permanently deletes one memory: its file, graph sidecar, archived copy and index rows; keep it on review.
Pin the release when launching (uvx halflife-mcp@0.1.2) so only the reviewed version runs; maintenance (archiving faded memories, expiring old traces) runs on the first write call.

The server makes no network calls of its own. For vector search, launch uvx --with fastembed --with numpy halflife-mcp@0.1.2 (keeps this package identity); the model downloads once; HALFLIFE_EMBED=off disables it.
Serve over stdio. The --http mode has no authentication and refuses non-loopback hosts unless --allow-network is passed.
